What MDM Remote Wipe / EraseDevice actually does — listing honesty

Apple ships EraseDevice as an MDM command for managed iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Apple TV devices enrolled through MDM. When an IT admin issues Remote Wipe, the device is erased remotely — removing apps, settings, and data per policy. On consumer-owned hardware with Find My enabled, erase may trigger Activation Lock; on organization-owned supervised hardware, Return to Service may follow wipe in some fleet workflows. Third-party MDM and device-management apps may complement this by surfacing Remote Wipe in admin consoles, documenting fleet erase workflows, or educating admins about lost-device response. AppLocale rewrites listing copy from what your US page already claims:

  • If your app aligns with MDM fleet workflows — description and screenshot overlays should name the benefits you deliver (远程抹掉, 抹掉设备, 远程清除) in commerce-idiomatic Chinese, not generic "wipe any iPhone instantly" overclaims.

  • Separate Remote Wipe from Activation Lock in copy — Activation Lock prevents consumer reactivation without the owner's Apple ID after erase; Remote Wipe is the MDM admin command that initiates erase. Remote wipe may trigger Activation Lock — but Activation Lock is not the wipe command story unless your English source leads with post-erase Apple ID gates.

Remote Wipe–specific vocabulary — what translates differently in zh-Hans

MDM admin-erase marketing on App Store pages uses vocabulary general localization guides rarely cover. zh-Hans copy should reflect how Chinese App Store readers evaluate Remote Wipe — not a literal paste of US marketing:

远程抹掉 (Remote Wipe)

Apple's Chinese MDM and enterprise support materials use 远程抹掉 for the MDM admin command that remotely erases a managed device. Some fleet-admin marketing also uses MDM 远程抹掉 when emphasizing the command path from an admin console. AppLocale picks the term IT admins recognize on each screenshot — an admin console frame needs 远程抹掉-friendly phrasing; a benefit headline may use MDM 远程抹掉 when accurate to your English source.

远程擦除 (remote erase)

US pages use "Remote erase" or "Remotely erase managed devices." China storefront copy often uses 远程擦除 when describing the MDM admin action that clears device data from a fleet console — distinct from Return to Service 返回服务 (erase plus return) and from Find My consumer erase flows. AppLocale aligns phrasing with your actual scope.

抹掉设备 (wipe device)

Short overlay lines and subtitle candidates often use 抹掉设备 when the English source says "Wipe device" or "Erase device" on a gallery frame showing the MDM admin confirmation dialog. Fits the 30-character subtitle cap when Remote Wipe is the lead benefit.

Some MDM vendors and Apple enterprise docs use 远程清除 as an alternate phrasing for remotely clearing managed device data. AppLocale picks 远程抹掉, 远程擦除, or 远程清除 based on your English source and the frame context — all signal MDM admin erase, not consumer Find My locate workflows.

AppLocale FAQ

What is MDM Remote Wipe / Erase Device and why does listing copy matter?

Remote Wipe is an MDM admin command (EraseDevice) that remotely erases a managed device. Marketing that workflow on your en-US page does not auto-fill zh-Hans Connect fields.

Does MDM EraseDevice support auto-translate my China listing?

No. Remote Wipe is an MDM admin command — it does not create or fill a Simplified Chinese localization row. Empty or English zh-Hans fields mean China buyers see en-US fallback on the product page.

What listing fields does AppLocale rewrite for Remote Wipe apps?

Paste-ready Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans) copy for App Store Connect listing fields you specify: title, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text when included, and screenshot overlay or caption lines that mention Remote Wipe, MDM EraseDevice, remote erase, or wipe device — rewritten from your English originals with terms like 远程抹掉, 远程擦除, and 抹掉设备 where accurate.

How is this different from Return to Service?

Remote Wipe listing copy markets the MDM admin erase command alone — wipe or factory-reset a managed device remotely. Return to Service listing copy markets erase plus return to a service-ready re-enrollment state for supervised fleet redeployment. Wipe-only vs wipe-plus-return — different zh-Hans vocabulary.

How is this different from Activation Lock or Find My Lost Mode?

Remote Wipe listing copy markets the MDM admin command that erases managed device data. Activation Lock listing copy markets the consumer Apple ID activation barrier that may appear after erase. Find My and Lost Mode help locate missing devices on a map — not MDM admin erase. Remote wipe may trigger Activation Lock — but Activation Lock is not the wipe command story unless your English source leads with post-erase Apple ID gates.

How is this different from Stolen Device Protection or Lockdown Mode?

Remote Wipe erases managed devices via MDM admin command. Stolen Device Protection adds biometric gates and Security Delay when away from familiar locations. Lockdown Mode is extreme cyberattack hardening. Each is a separate Apple feature — do not reuse boilerplate across them.
